The 30 questions in this guide build from foundational concepts to the advanced topics that distinguish senior Node.js engineers. To solidify your preparation, build a production-ready Node.js API: implement proper error handling, request validation, authentication middleware, connection pooling, structured logging, and graceful shutdown. Profile it under load with autocannon. Add clustering for multi-core utilization. Write unit and integration tests. Deploy it with Docker. This real-world experience, combined with the theoretical foundation this guide provides, will give you the depth and confidence to excel in any Node.js interview.

faq.question: What is the Node.js event loop and how does it work?
faq.answer: The event loop is Node.js's mechanism for handling asynchronous operations without blocking the main thread. It has six phases: timers (setTimeout/setInterval callbacks), pending callbacks (I/O callbacks deferred to next iteration), idle/prepare (internal), poll (retrieving new I/O events), check (setImmediate callbacks), and close callbacks. Between phases, Node.js checks the microtask queues — process.nextTick (highest priority) and Promise microtasks — and processes all of them before moving to the next phase. This enables Node.js to handle thousands of concurrent I/O operations efficiently.

faq.question: What is the difference between process.nextTick and setImmediate?
faq.answer: process.nextTick callbacks run after the current operation completes but before the event loop continues to its next phase — they execute between phases, with higher priority than Promises. setImmediate callbacks run in the check phase of the event loop, after I/O events. In practice, process.nextTick fires sooner than setImmediate. Use process.nextTick when you need a callback to run before any I/O in the current iteration. Prefer setImmediate for most async patterns to avoid starving the I/O phase (recursive process.nextTick calls block I/O).

faq.question: What are Node.js streams and why are they important?
faq.answer: Streams are objects that enable processing data piece by piece rather than loading it all into memory. There are four types: Readable (source of data, e.g. fs.createReadStream), Writable (data destination, e.g. fs.createWriteStream), Duplex (both readable and writable, e.g. TCP socket), and Transform (modifies data while passing through, e.g. zlib compression). Streams are critical for processing large files, HTTP responses, real-time data, and database cursors without memory overflow. Use stream.pipeline() to connect streams with proper error handling.

faq.question: How do you scale a Node.js application?
faq.answer: Scaling strategies for Node.js: 1) Cluster module — forks multiple worker processes equal to CPU count, each running on the same port, handled by the OS load balancer. PM2 automates this. 2) Horizontal scaling — run multiple Node.js instances behind a load balancer (Nginx, AWS ALB). 3) Worker Threads — for CPU-bound work within a single process. 4) Caching — Redis for session data, computed results, and rate limiting to reduce database load. 5) Database connection pooling — limit concurrent connections. 6) Message queues — decouple heavy processing from the request cycle.

faq.question: What are common security vulnerabilities in Node.js applications?
faq.answer: Common Node.js security vulnerabilities: 1) Injection attacks (SQL, NoSQL, command injection) — use parameterized queries and input validation with Joi/Zod. 2) ReDoS — catastrophic backtracking in regular expressions under malicious input — use safe-regex. 3) Path traversal — user-controlled file paths accessing unauthorized files — always resolve and validate paths. 4) Prototype pollution — malicious input modifying Object.prototype — use Object.create(null) for unvalidated data. 5) Dependency vulnerabilities — run npm audit regularly, use Snyk or Dependabot. 6) Sensitive data exposure — use Helmet.js for security headers, never log sensitive data.

seo.title: Top 30 Express.js Interview Questions and Answers (2026) – Full Guide
seo.meta_description: Prepare for Express.js interviews with 30 expert Q&As covering middleware, routing, error handling, security, REST API design, authentication, and Express best practices.
seo.og_description: Master Express.js interviews with 30 expert Q&As on middleware, routing, authentication, REST API design, error handling, and security for Node.js developers.

content.introduction: Express.js has been the de facto standard for building Node.js web applications and APIs for over a decade. Its minimalist, unopinionated design — providing just routing, middleware, and HTTP utilities without imposing a structure — gives developers the flexibility to architect their applications as needed while benefiting from a stable, battle-tested foundation. Despite the emergence of newer frameworks like Fastify (which offers superior performance), Koa (from the Express creators), Hapi, and NestJS (which uses Express or Fastify under the hood), Express remains the most widely used Node.js framework by an enormous margin. Its ubiquity means Express knowledge is expected in virtually every Node.js developer interview. This guide covers the top 30 Express.js interview questions for 2026, covering everything from Express application setup and routing basics for beginners, through middleware architecture and error handling for intermediate developers, to security hardening, performance optimization, and production best practices for senior engineers. Understanding Express deeply means understanding not just its API but the middleware pattern, request/response cycle, and how to build maintainable, secure, and performant APIs — skills that are directly applicable to any Node.js web framework.

sections.heading: Express.js in the Modern Node.js Ecosystem
sections.content: Express.js's longevity in the Node.js ecosystem is a testament to the power of simplicity and stability. Released in 2010, Express introduced the middleware pipeline concept to Node.js development — a pattern so effective that virtually every Node.js framework that followed either built on Express directly or adopted the same pattern. Express version 4 (still the production standard) introduced isolated routers, allowing large applications to be organized into modular route handlers. Express 5 (in long-term alpha/beta) brings native Promise support, better error propagation, and an updated path matching syntax. While Fastify has become the performance-sensitive developer's choice (benchmarks show it handling 2–3x more requests per second than Express), and NestJS has captured the enterprise TypeScript market, Express's simplicity makes it the best framework for learning REST API development fundamentals. Many developers working with NestJS, which uses Express or Fastify as its HTTP adapter, benefit from understanding Express middleware patterns since NestJS interceptors, guards, and pipes conceptually mirror Express middleware. For interviews, Express knowledge signals a strong understanding of the HTTP request/response cycle, middleware composition, and REST API design principles that are transferable across all web frameworks.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for an Express.js Interview
sections.content: Express.js interview preparation should be grounded in understanding the request/response cycle and middleware composition, not just memorizing API methods. Start with the basics: creating an Express app, defining routes (app.get, app.post, app.put, app.delete, app.patch), request object properties (req.params, req.query, req.body, req.headers, req.cookies), and response methods (res.send, res.json, res.status, res.redirect, res.render). Middleware is the heart of Express — understand that every function with (req, res, next) signature is middleware, how app.use() mounts middleware globally or at a path prefix, the order of middleware execution, and the four key uses of middleware (logging, parsing, authentication, error handling). Error-handling middleware has four parameters (err, req, res, next) and must be registered last. Express Router enables modular route organization — critical for any non-trivial application. Study authentication patterns: session-based auth with express-session, JWT-based stateless auth with jsonwebtoken (sign, verify, middleware to protect routes). Input validation with Joi, Yup, or express-validator. CORS configuration with cors middleware. Security best practices with Helmet.js. File upload handling with multer. Understand how to properly test Express APIs with Supertest and Jest or Vitest.

sections.heading: Beginner Express.js Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Beginner Express questions test fundamental understanding of what Express is and how to build a basic API. Key topics: installing Express (npm install express), creating an application instance (const app = express()), starting a server (app.listen(3000)), defining GET and POST routes, using route parameters (:id in the path), query string parsing (automatically available on req.query), parsing JSON request bodies (app.use(express.json())), serving static files (app.use(express.static('public'))), and the basics of the middleware chain. Freshers should understand the concept of the middleware pipeline: each middleware function receives req, res, and next, and can modify req/res or call next() to pass control to the next middleware. If a middleware does not call next() and does not send a response, the request hangs. A common beginner question is the difference between app.use() and app.get() — app.use() matches any HTTP method and can match path prefixes; app.get() only matches GET requests and the exact path (or exact prefix with router). Basic response types: res.json() sends JSON with correct Content-Type header; res.send() auto-detects content type; res.status(404).json({error:'Not found'}) sets status and sends JSON in one chain.

sections.heading: Intermediate Express.js Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Intermediate Express questions focus on real-world API patterns: authentication, validation, error handling, and code organization. Express Router is the primary organizational tool: create a router instance (express.Router()), define routes on it, export it, and mount it in the main app (app.use('/api/users', userRouter)). This enables feature-based code organization. JWT authentication middleware pattern: extract token from Authorization header (Bearer token), verify with jsonwebtoken.verify(), attach decoded user to req.user, and call next() — or return 401 if invalid. Error handling requires a dedicated four-parameter middleware registered after all routes. It catches errors thrown with next(error) or thrown in async route handlers (in Express 5, uncaught async errors are forwarded automatically; in Express 4, you must catch and call next(err) explicitly). Input validation middleware using express-validator or Joi schema validation catches invalid requests before they reach route logic. Rate limiting with express-rate-limit protects against brute force and DoS attacks. Understanding HTTP status codes semantics — 200 OK, 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 429 Too Many Requests, 500 Internal Server Error — and using them correctly in API responses is expected at this level.

sections.heading: Advanced Express.js Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Advanced Express questions cover security hardening, performance, testing strategies, and architectural patterns for large APIs. Security is the primary advanced topic: Helmet.js sets 14+ HTTP security headers automatically (X-XSS-Protection, Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, X-Frame-Options). CORS must be carefully configured — use the cors package with an allowlist of trusted origins rather than wildcard * in production. SQL injection prevention: never concatenate user input into queries — always use parameterized queries or ORM methods. NoSQL injection in MongoDB: validate that user-controlled values in queries are not objects (which could inject $where operators). HTTP parameter pollution: use hpp middleware to prevent polluted query parameters. Denial of service: express-rate-limit, request size limits (express.json({ limit: '10kb' })), and timeout middleware prevent various attack vectors. For performance: minimize middleware stack, use compression middleware (gzip/Brotli with the compression package), implement HTTP caching headers (Cache-Control, ETag) for GET responses, and use connection pooling for databases. Structured logging with Winston or Pino (faster than Winston) with request correlation IDs for distributed tracing. Graceful shutdown: handle SIGTERM by stopping new connections, completing in-flight requests, then closing database connections before exiting.

sections.heading: Testing Express.js Applications: Best Practices
sections.content: Testing is increasingly evaluated in backend interviews, and Express has excellent testing support. The primary tool for testing Express APIs is Supertest, which creates an HTTP server from your Express app and allows making real HTTP requests in tests without binding to a port. This enables fast, isolated API endpoint testing. Test structure: unit tests for individual middleware functions and utility functions, integration tests for route handlers (testing the full middleware stack for a route using Supertest), and end-to-end tests for complete user flows. The key architectural practice for testability is separating the Express app configuration (app.js) from server startup (server.js) — Supertest imports app.js directly without starting the server. Dependency injection or service layer patterns make business logic independently testable without HTTP overhead. Mock database connections in integration tests using in-memory databases (better-sqlite3 for SQLite, mongodb-memory-server for MongoDB) or test containers (docker containers with real databases). Snapshot testing of API response shapes with Jest ensures API contracts are not accidentally broken. Test coverage: focus on covering all route variations, error scenarios, authentication/authorization paths, and edge cases in input validation. Use factory functions for test data generation to keep tests maintainable.

content.conclusion: Express.js's elegant simplicity — give it a function, it calls it when a request arrives — has made it one of the most influential frameworks in web development history. Mastering Express means mastering the fundamentals of HTTP, middleware composition, REST API design, and backend security that underpin all web frameworks. The 30 questions in this guide prepare you thoroughly for Express interviews at every level. Build a complete RESTful API with Express: implement CRUD operations, JWT authentication, input validation, proper error handling, rate limiting, and helmet security headers. Write comprehensive tests with Supertest. Document your API with Swagger/OpenAPI. Deploy it with Docker. This hands-on experience, reflecting real production practices, will make your Express knowledge interview-ready and immediately valuable to employers.

faq.question: What is middleware in Express.js?
faq.answer: Middleware in Express is a function with the signature (req, res, next) that has access to the request and response objects and the next middleware in the pipeline. Middleware can: execute code, modify req/res objects, end the request/response cycle (send a response), or call next() to pass control to the next middleware. Types: application-level (app.use()), router-level (router.use()), error-handling (4 parameters: err, req, res, next), built-in (express.json(), express.static()), and third-party (cors, helmet, morgan).

faq.question: How do you handle errors in Express.js?
faq.answer: Express uses a special 4-parameter middleware for error handling: app.use((err, req, res, next) => {...}). Register it after all routes. In Express 4, catch async errors and pass them to next(err): route handler wraps async function in try/catch and calls next(err) in the catch block. In Express 5, async errors propagate automatically. For operational errors (known, expected), send appropriate HTTP status codes. For programming errors (unexpected), log them and send 500. Use a centralized error handler that classifies error types and responds consistently.

faq.question: What is the difference between app.use() and app.get() in Express?
faq.answer: app.use() mounts middleware that responds to all HTTP methods and matches path prefixes — app.use('/api', router) matches /api, /api/users, /api/products/123. app.get() (and post, put, delete, patch) only matches that specific HTTP method and performs exact path matching (or uses route parameters). app.use() is for middleware and sub-router mounting; app.get() etc. are for defining specific route handlers. Both can take middleware functions — app.get('/users', authMiddleware, getUsers) chains middleware for that specific route.

faq.question: How do you implement JWT authentication in Express?
faq.answer: JWT authentication flow: 1) Login route validates credentials, signs a JWT (jsonwebtoken.sign({userId}, secret, {expiresIn:'1h'})), and returns it. 2) Client stores the token and sends it in the Authorization header (Bearer <token>) on subsequent requests. 3) Auth middleware extracts the token (req.headers.authorization.split(' ')[1]), verifies it (jsonwebtoken.verify(token, secret)), attaches the decoded payload to req.user, and calls next(). If verification fails, return 401. 4) Protect routes by adding the auth middleware before route handlers.

faq.question: How do you make Express.js more secure?
faq.answer: Key Express security practices: 1) Use Helmet.js to set security HTTP headers automatically. 2) Configure CORS with explicit origin allowlists, not wildcard *. 3) Validate and sanitize all user input with Joi, Zod, or express-validator. 4) Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL/NoSQL injection. 5) Implement rate limiting with express-rate-limit. 6) Set body size limits (express.json({limit: '10kb'})). 7) Use HTTPS with proper TLS configuration. 8) Store secrets in environment variables, never in code. 9) Keep dependencies updated and run npm audit regularly. 10) Implement proper error handling that does not leak stack traces to clients.

seo.title: Top 30 Python Interview Questions and Answers (2026) – Beginner to Advanced
seo.meta_description: Ace your Python interview with 30 expert Q&As covering data structures, OOP, decorators, generators, async programming, memory management, and Python 3.12+ features.
seo.og_description: From basic syntax to advanced decorators, generators, async/await, and memory management — master Python interviews with 30 comprehensive Q&As.

content.introduction: Python continues to reign as one of the world's most popular and versatile programming languages in 2026. Its clean syntax, extensive standard library, and massive ecosystem of third-party packages have made it the language of choice for web development (Django, FastAPI, Flask), data science and machine learning (NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, PyTorch), automation and scripting, DevOps tooling, and backend API development. Python 3.12 brought significant performance improvements — CPython is now 1.25x faster than Python 3.10 on average — and features like improved error messages, the new type parameter syntax (PEP 695), and the @override decorator. Python interviews have grown significantly more sophisticated, with companies now testing not just syntax knowledge but deep understanding of Python's object model, memory management, concurrency models, and performance characteristics. This guide covers 30 Python interview questions across all levels: from core syntax and data structures for freshers to advanced topics like descriptors, metaclasses, the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), asyncio, and Cython for senior engineers. Whether you are targeting a Python web developer role, a backend engineer position, or a Python-adjacent data engineering role, this guide provides the depth and breadth you need.

sections.heading: Why Python Is the Most Versatile Language in 2026
sections.content: Python's versatility is unmatched in the programming landscape. It is simultaneously the preferred language for machine learning research (PyTorch, JAX), production ML systems (TensorFlow Serving, ONNX Runtime), web APIs (FastAPI has become the fastest-growing Python web framework), data engineering (Apache Spark's PySpark API, Apache Airflow for orchestration), scientific computing (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib), DevOps and infrastructure (Ansible, Terraform providers, AWS CDK), and general scripting. This breadth means Python developers have extraordinary career flexibility — skills developed in one domain transfer to others. The Python Package Index (PyPI) hosts over 500,000 packages, providing a solution for virtually any problem. Python's adoption in education — it has displaced Java as the most taught first programming language at universities globally — means the talent pool is large and the learning resources are abundant. For interviewers, Python fluency has different meanings depending on the role: a web developer interview focuses on frameworks and async patterns; a data engineer interview focuses on data structures and functional programming; a backend interview focuses on OOP, testing, and API design. This guide's comprehensive coverage prepares you for all these contexts.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for a Python Interview
sections.content: Python interview preparation requires different focus areas depending on the role. For general Python developer roles, master: Python's built-in data structures (list, dict, set, tuple) and their time complexities, list/dict/set comprehensions, lambda functions, map/filter/zip built-ins, OOP in Python (classes, inheritance, multiple inheritance with MRO, dunder/magic methods), file I/O and context managers (with statement), exception handling (try/except/else/finally), modules and packages, and the standard library (collections, itertools, functools, os, sys, pathlib). Intermediate preparation: decorators (function decorators with and without arguments, class decorators), generators and iterators (yield, yield from, next(), iter()), context managers (contextlib.contextmanager), the functools module (lru_cache, partial, reduce), and Python's type hints system with mypy or pyright for type checking. Advanced preparation: Python's memory model (CPython reference counting, garbage collector for cycles, memory views), the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) and its implications for multithreading vs multiprocessing, asyncio and async/await for I/O-bound concurrency, descriptors (__get__, __set__, __delete__), metaclasses (type as the metaclass of all classes), and performance profiling with cProfile and memory_profiler. Practice LeetCode problems specifically in Python, focusing on Pythonic solutions using built-ins.

sections.heading: Beginner Python Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Beginner Python questions focus on language fundamentals and Python's key data structures. Core topics: the difference between mutable and immutable types (lists are mutable, tuples are immutable — tuples can be used as dictionary keys because they are hashable), Python's dynamic typing and how to use type hints (def greet(name: str) -> str), string methods and formatting (f-strings are the preferred modern approach), list operations (indexing, slicing, append, extend, insert, remove, pop), dictionary operations (dict.get with default, dict.items, dict.keys, dict.values, dict comprehensions), set operations (union, intersection, difference), and control flow (for loops including enumerate and zip, while, if/elif/else, list comprehensions as a Pythonic alternative to for loops). Understanding that Python passes objects by assignment — for mutable objects, mutations affect all references; for immutable objects, reassignment creates a new object — is a common beginner interview question. The difference between == (value equality) and is (identity — same object in memory) is also frequently tested. Python's None type and how to check for it (always use is None not == None, since a custom __eq__ could make something equal None).

sections.heading: Intermediate Python Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Intermediate Python questions assess mastery of Python's powerful higher-level features. Decorators are a major topic: a decorator is a function that takes a function and returns a modified version. The @functools.wraps decorator preserves the wrapped function's metadata. Decorators with arguments require an extra nesting level. Class-based decorators implement __call__. Common built-in decorators: @property (converts a method to an attribute), @staticmethod (method that does not receive self), @classmethod (receives the class as first argument for factory methods). Generators enable lazy evaluation — functions with yield return an iterator that produces values one at a time instead of building the full list in memory. yield from delegates to another generator. Generator expressions (x*2 for x in range(1000)) are memory-efficient list comprehension alternatives. Context managers implement __enter__ and __exit__ for resource management — the with statement guarantees cleanup even on exceptions. The collections module: Counter (frequency counting), defaultdict (avoids KeyError for missing keys), OrderedDict (before Python 3.7 guaranteed ordering), deque (O(1) append/pop from both ends), namedtuple (lightweight immutable objects). itertools for memory-efficient iteration: chain, product, permutations, combinations, groupby, islice.

sections.heading: Advanced Python Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Advanced Python topics for senior developers cover the language's internals and concurrency model. The Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is Python's most discussed limitation: it is a mutex that allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time in CPython. This makes Python threads ineffective for CPU-bound parallelism (multiple threads run on one core). Solutions: multiprocessing module (bypasses GIL with separate processes and separate memory), concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor (high-level multiprocessing), and for I/O-bound concurrency, threading or asyncio both work well despite the GIL (I/O releases the GIL). asyncio provides single-threaded concurrent I/O: event loop, coroutines (async def functions), await for suspending, asyncio.gather for concurrent coroutines, asyncio.create_task for background tasks, and async context managers/iterators. Descriptors (__get__, __set__, __delete__) are the mechanism behind properties, classmethods, staticmethods, and many ORM field implementations. Metaclasses: every class is an instance of type (its metaclass). Custom metaclasses can modify class creation — used in ORMs (SQLAlchemy, Django models) to transform class attributes into database columns. Python's data model: dunder methods (__repr__, __str__, __len__, __getitem__, __setitem__, __iter__, __next__, __enter__, __exit__, __eq__, __hash__, __slots__) control how objects behave with built-in functions and operators.

sections.heading: Python in Web Development and Data Engineering Interviews
sections.content: Python's versatility means interview preparation differs significantly by role. For Python web development interviews (Django, FastAPI, Flask): understand ORM patterns (Django ORM vs SQLAlchemy), RESTful API design with Django REST Framework or FastAPI (which uses type hints for automatic validation and documentation), async web frameworks (FastAPI with Starlette, async SQLAlchemy), authentication patterns (JWT with PyJWT, OAuth2 with FastAPI), middleware patterns, and testing with pytest and httpx for async API testing. For data engineering interviews: pandas DataFrames and Series operations (groupby, merge, pivot, apply), NumPy array operations and broadcasting, writing efficient vectorized code instead of Python loops, memory optimization (using appropriate dtypes, chunked reading with chunksize), PySpark for distributed data processing (RDDs vs DataFrames, transformations vs actions, lazy evaluation), and pipeline orchestration concepts with Airflow (DAGs, operators, sensors, hooks). For backend engineering interviews: Python's performance characteristics, profiling (cProfile, line_profiler), Celery for async task queues, Redis integration (redis-py), SQLAlchemy ORM and Core for database abstraction, Alembic for migrations, and containerizing Python applications with Docker.

content.conclusion: Python's combination of readable syntax, powerful standard library, and massive ecosystem makes it one of the most rewarding languages to master deeply. The journey from knowing Python syntax to truly understanding its object model, memory management, concurrency patterns, and idiomatic style is the journey this guide supports. The 30 questions here prepare you for Python interviews across the full spectrum of difficulty and specialization. To solidify your preparation, solve 50 LeetCode problems in Python focusing on Pythonic solutions, build a FastAPI or Django REST API with proper testing, and experiment with asyncio for a real async programming challenge. Read Python Enhancement Proposals (PEPs) — especially PEP 8 (style), PEP 20 (Zen of Python), PEP 484 (type hints), and PEP 525 (async generators). This depth of engagement with the language will show in your interview answers and set you apart from candidates who only know the surface.

faq.question: What are Python decorators and how do they work?
faq.answer: A decorator is a higher-order function that takes a function as input and returns a modified version. The @decorator syntax is syntactic sugar: @my_decorator above def func() is equivalent to func = my_decorator(func). Decorators are used for logging, timing, authentication, caching (@functools.lru_cache), and input validation. Decorators with arguments require triple nesting: the outermost function takes arguments, returns a decorator, which takes the function and returns the wrapper. Use @functools.wraps(func) in the wrapper to preserve the original function's __name__ and __doc__.

faq.question: What is the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in Python?
faq.answer: The GIL is a mutex in CPython that ensures only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, even on multi-core systems. This simplifies CPython's memory management (reference counting is not thread-safe without the GIL) but limits CPU-bound multithreading. For CPU-bound parallelism, use the multiprocessing module (separate processes, each with their own GIL). For I/O-bound concurrency, threading or asyncio both work well since I/O operations release the GIL. Python 3.13 is introducing an experimental no-GIL build.

faq.question: What is the difference between a list and a tuple in Python?
faq.answer: Lists are mutable (can be modified after creation), enclosed in [], and have methods like append, remove, pop. Tuples are immutable (cannot be modified), enclosed in (), and are hashable (can be dictionary keys or set members). Tuples are slightly more memory-efficient and faster to create than lists. Use lists for sequences that will change; use tuples for fixed collections (coordinates, RGB values, function return values). Named tuples (collections.namedtuple) provide attribute access to tuple elements, combining tuple immutability with record-like readability.

faq.question: What are generators in Python and when should you use them?
faq.answer: Generators are functions that use yield to return values one at a time instead of building the complete list in memory. They implement the iterator protocol lazily. Use generators when: processing large datasets that do not fit in memory (read a file line by line with yield), implementing infinite sequences (Fibonacci numbers), creating data pipelines where each step yields to the next, and anywhere a list comprehension would create a large intermediate list. yield from delegates to another generator/iterable. Generator expressions (x for x in range(n)) are the compact form for simple cases.

faq.question: How does Python's memory management work?
faq.answer: CPython uses reference counting as the primary memory management mechanism: each object tracks how many references point to it, and when the count drops to zero, the object is immediately deallocated. This provides predictable, incremental deallocation. A cyclic garbage collector (gc module) handles reference cycles (objects referencing each other) that reference counting cannot clean up. The memory allocator uses an arena system with three tiers: the OS allocator for large objects (>512 bytes), pymalloc for small objects (<=512 bytes), and a free list for frequently created/destroyed objects like small integers (-5 to 256 are cached).

seo.title: Top 30 Django Interview Questions and Answers (2026) – Full Stack Guide
seo.meta_description: Ace your Django interview with 30 expert Q&As covering Django ORM, REST framework, authentication, signals, caching, security, middleware, and Django 5+ features.
seo.og_description: Master Django interviews with 30 expert Q&As on MVT architecture, ORM, DRF, authentication, caching, signals, and security for Python developers.

content.introduction: Django remains one of the most respected and widely used Python web frameworks in 2026, trusted by organizations ranging from Instagram (which famously runs on Django at massive scale) to the Washington Post, Disqus, Bitbucket, and thousands of SaaS companies globally. Django's 'batteries-included' philosophy — providing a production-ready ORM, authentication system, admin interface, form handling, security middleware, internationalization support, and much more out of the box — makes it the go-to framework for developers who want to build full-featured web applications quickly without assembling dozens of third-party packages. Django 5.0 and 5.1 introduced significant improvements: facet filters in the admin, simplified queryset API improvements, async ORM support (alongside the existing sync API), and improved ASGI performance. Django REST Framework (DRF) continues to be the standard for building RESTful APIs with Django, while Django Ninja (FastAPI-inspired, type-annotation-based) has emerged as a popular, higher-performance API alternative. This guide covers 30 Django interview questions for 2026, from the MVT architecture and ORM basics for beginners through signals, custom managers, and caching for intermediate developers to performance optimization, async Django, and security hardening for senior engineers.

sections.heading: Why Django Powers Enterprise Python Web Development
sections.content: Django's design philosophy — explicit over implicit, convention over configuration, DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) — has made it the foundation of some of the world's highest-traffic Python applications. Instagram famously runs on Django and has served as proof that Django can scale to hundreds of millions of users with proper architecture. The Django ORM's ability to abstract complex database queries while generating optimized SQL, combined with its migration system for schema version control, solves two of the hardest problems in web application development — data modeling and schema evolution — in an elegant, developer-friendly way. Django's built-in admin interface provides an automatically generated, customizable management dashboard from model definitions alone — reducing the development time for internal tools to near zero. Django's security defaults are industry-leading: CSRF protection, SQL injection prevention via parameterized queries, XSS prevention through automatic template escaping, clickjacking protection, and password hashing with PBKDF2/Argon2 are all enabled or available by default. For organizations prioritizing security compliance (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2), Django's security track record and Django Security Team's rapid response to vulnerabilities provide important assurance. The Django community's ecosystem — thousands of reusable apps for payments (django-stripe), social auth (django-allauth), REST APIs (djangorestframework), filtering (django-filter), full-text search (django-elasticsearch-dsl), and more — accelerates development further.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for a Django Interview
sections.content: Django interview preparation should cover the framework's full stack: from the request/response cycle and MVT architecture to production deployment patterns. Start with the MVT (Model-View-Template) pattern: Models define data structure (Django ORM mapped to database tables), Views handle business logic and return HTTP responses (function-based views or class-based views), Templates render HTML from context data. Master the Django ORM: creating models, field types (CharField, IntegerField, ForeignKey, ManyToManyField, OneToOneField), Meta class (ordering, indexes, constraints), QuerySet API (filter, exclude, get, create, update, delete, select_related, prefetch_related, annotate, aggregate, Q objects, F expressions), migrations (makemigrations, migrate, squashmigrations, data migrations). URL routing: urlpatterns in urls.py, path() and re_path(), include() for modular URL organization, named URLs with reverse(), namespace support. Django REST Framework: Serializers (ModelSerializer, nested serializers, validated_data), ViewSets (ModelViewSet, CRUD in 40 lines), Routers (auto-generate URL patterns), Permissions (IsAuthenticated, IsAdminUser, custom permissions), Authentication (TokenAuthentication, JWT with djangorestframework-simplejwt, SessionAuthentication), Filtering (django-filter integration), Pagination. Signals (post_save, pre_delete) for decoupled side effects. Caching (database, file-based, Redis/Memcached cache backends with cache.set/get/delete).

sections.heading: Beginner Django Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Beginner Django questions test your understanding of Django's core architecture and how to build a basic web application or API. Key beginner topics: Django's MVT pattern and how it differs from MVC (in MVT, the View handles controller logic and the Template is the view layer), creating a new Django project (django-admin startproject) and app (python manage.py startapp), the Django development server (python manage.py runserver), how models map to database tables (each model class becomes a database table, each field becomes a column), creating and applying migrations (makemigrations generates migration files from model changes; migrate applies them), the Django admin (register models with admin.site.register(MyModel)), basic CRUD with the Django shell (python manage.py shell), function-based views (a Python function taking request and returning HttpResponse or JsonResponse), URL configuration and routing, and the settings.py file (INSTALLED_APPS, DATABASES, TEMPLATES, DEBUG, SECRET_KEY, ALLOWED_HOSTS). Freshers should also understand Django's ORM query API: MyModel.objects.all(), MyModel.objects.filter(field=value), MyModel.objects.get(pk=1), MyModel.objects.create(**data). Understanding the difference between filter() (returns QuerySet) and get() (returns single object or raises exception) is a very common beginner question.

sections.heading: Intermediate Django Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Intermediate Django questions assess depth in the ORM, Django REST Framework, and application patterns. ORM performance is a key intermediate topic: the N+1 query problem occurs when a query for a list of objects is followed by N individual queries for related objects. Fix with select_related() for ForeignKey/OneToOne (SQL JOIN) or prefetch_related() for ManyToMany/reverse ForeignKey (separate query with Python-side joining). Use only() to limit fields fetched, defer() to defer heavy fields, values() for dict results, and values_list() for tuple results. Explain how QuerySets are lazy (no database hit until evaluated) and when they are evaluated (iteration, len(), bool(), slicing, list(), str()). Django REST Framework serializers: ModelSerializer auto-generates fields from the model, validate_<field> methods for field-level validation, validate() for cross-field validation, create() and update() for custom save logic, and nested serializers for related data. Class-based views: the View hierarchy, APIView in DRF, mixins (CreateModelMixin, ListModelMixin, etc.), GenericAPIView, and the convenience ViewSet/ModelViewSet. Custom permissions (has_permission for view-level, has_object_permission for object-level). Signal-based decoupled side effects: post_save signal to send welcome emails after user creation.

sections.heading: Advanced Django Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Advanced Django questions target senior developers and architects. Custom model managers and QuerySets enable business logic encapsulation: class PublishedManager(models.Manager): def get_queryset(self): return super().get_queryset().filter(status='published'). Custom managers provide model-level APIs that express domain language. Database transactions: Django's atomic() decorator/context manager ensures a block of database operations either all succeed or all roll back. Savepoints for nested transactions. select_for_update() for row-level locking in concurrent environments. Async Django: Django 4.1+ supports async views (async def my_view(request)), async ORM (sync_to_async wrapper or async QuerySet API in Django 4.2+), and async middleware. ASGI deployment with uvicorn or daphne enables true async performance for WebSocket and long-polling endpoints. Django Channels for WebSocket support. Caching strategies: per-view caching (@cache_page), template fragment caching ({% cache %}), low-level cache API (cache.set/get) with Redis backend for high performance and cache invalidation. Content types framework for generic relations. Custom form fields and widgets for complex input types. Multi-database routing for read replicas. Database-level full-text search with Django's SearchVector, SearchQuery, SearchRank (PostgreSQL).

sections.heading: Django Security and Production Deployment Best Practices
sections.content: Security and deployment knowledge are critical for senior Django interviews. Django's built-in security features: CSRF middleware (automatically protects POST/PUT/DELETE forms and DRF endpoints), SQL injection prevention (ORM always uses parameterized queries — never use raw() with user input), XSS prevention (template auto-escaping — mark safe only trusted content), clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options: DENY via XFrameOptionsMiddleware), HTTPS enforcement (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, HSTS via SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS), Content Security Policy (django-csp package), and password hashing (Django's AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS and PBKDF2/Argon2 hashers). Production deployment checklist: DEBUG=False, SECRET_KEY from environment variable (not hardcoded), ALLOWED_HOSTS set correctly, database using PostgreSQL (not SQLite), static files served by Nginx or a CDN (collectstatic), media files on cloud storage (django-storages with S3), logging configured for production (centralized logging with Sentry), and health check endpoints for load balancers. Docker containerization: Dockerfile with multi-stage builds (separate dependency installation from code copying for layer caching), gunicorn as the WSGI server, Nginx as reverse proxy for SSL termination and static file serving, environment variables managed with .env files (python-decouple or django-environ), and celery for async task processing with redis as broker.

content.conclusion: Django is a framework that rewards mastery with extraordinary productivity. Once you understand its conventions — models, migrations, views, URLs, templates, the ORM — you can build production-ready features in a fraction of the time they would take in a lower-level framework. The 30 questions in this guide prepare you for Django interviews from entry-level to senior architect. To prepare practically: build a complete Django REST API with DRF, implement JWT authentication, add role-based permissions, optimize a query-heavy endpoint by eliminating N+1 queries with select_related and prefetch_related, and deploy the application with Docker, gunicorn, and Nginx. Write comprehensive tests with pytest-django. These hands-on exercises reinforce every concept in this guide and give you real experiences to draw on when answering interview questions.

faq.question: What is Django's MVT architecture?
faq.answer: MVT stands for Model-View-Template. Model defines the data structure (maps to database tables via the ORM). View contains the business logic — receives HTTP requests, interacts with models, and returns HTTP responses (similar to the Controller in MVC). Template defines the presentation layer — HTML files with Django template language for rendering dynamic data. The difference from MVC: Django's View is MVC's Controller, and Django's Template is MVC's View. The URL dispatcher routes requests to the appropriate view.

faq.question: What is the N+1 query problem in Django and how do you fix it?
faq.answer: The N+1 problem occurs when fetching a list of N objects triggers N additional queries for related data. Example: for post in Post.objects.all(): print(post.author.name) — fetches all posts (1 query) then fetches each author separately (N queries). Fix with select_related() for ForeignKey/OneToOneField (Django performs a SQL JOIN): Post.objects.select_related('author').all(). For ManyToManyField or reverse ForeignKey, use prefetch_related() which does a separate query and joins in Python: Post.objects.prefetch_related('tags').all(). Use Django Debug Toolbar or django-silk to detect N+1 queries in development.

faq.question: What is Django REST Framework (DRF) and why is it used?
faq.answer: Django REST Framework is the most popular Django extension for building RESTful APIs. It provides: Serializers (convert model instances to/from JSON with validation), class-based views (APIView, GenericAPIView, ViewSets), an automatic browsable API interface, flexible authentication backends (Token, Session, JWT via third-party packages), permission classes, throttling, filtering, pagination, and versioning. ModelViewSet provides full CRUD in ~10 lines of code. The router auto-generates RESTful URL patterns from ViewSets. DRF dramatically reduces boilerplate for building standard REST APIs.

faq.question: How does Django's authentication system work?
faq.answer: Django's built-in authentication provides: User model (username, password, email, first_name, last_name, is_staff, is_superuser), authentication (authenticate(username, password) returns User or None), login/logout (login(request, user) stores user ID in session, logout() clears session), and access control (login_required decorator, PermissionRequiredMixin). For APIs, DRF adds Token authentication and integration with JWT packages (djangorestframework-simplejwt). Custom user models: always create a custom user model (extending AbstractUser or AbstractBaseUser) at project start — changing the user model later is complex.

faq.question: How do you improve Django application performance?
faq.answer: Django performance optimization strategies: 1) Database — eliminate N+1 with select_related/prefetch_related, add database indexes on frequently filtered fields, use only()/values() to limit selected columns, use bulk_create/bulk_update for mass operations. 2) Caching — cache expensive views with @cache_page, use Redis/Memcached for session and low-level caching, cache QuerySet results for read-heavy data. 3) Query optimization — use explain() to analyze query plans, avoid calling count() if exists() suffices. 4) Application — use Celery for background tasks, use connection pooling with PgBouncer for PostgreSQL. 5) Static assets — serve via CDN, enable compression, use django-compressor for JS/CSS minification.

seo.title: Top 30 Spring Boot Interview Questions and Answers (2026) – Java Backend Guide
seo.meta_description: Prepare for Spring Boot interviews with 30 expert Q&As covering auto-configuration, dependency injection, Spring Data JPA, REST APIs, security, microservices, and Spring Boot 3.
secondary_keywords: Spring Boot interview questions and answers
seo.og_description: Master Spring Boot interviews with 30 expert Q&As on auto-configuration, dependency injection, JPA, security, microservices, and Spring Boot 3+ features.

content.introduction: Spring Boot is the dominant framework for enterprise Java backend development in 2026, chosen by organizations ranging from Fortune 500 companies to high-growth startups for building microservices, REST APIs, batch processing systems, and event-driven applications. Spring Boot 3.x, built on Spring Framework 6 and requiring Java 17+, introduces virtual threads support (Project Loom integration), GraalVM native image compilation for near-instant startup times, improved observability with Micrometer, and a thoroughly modernized baseline. Spring Boot's core value proposition — eliminating the complex XML-based configuration of traditional Spring in favor of convention-over-configuration auto-configuration — has made enterprise Java development dramatically more productive. This guide covers the top 30 Spring Boot interview questions for 2026, from foundational concepts like dependency injection, auto-configuration, and Spring annotations for beginners, to intermediate topics like Spring Data JPA, Spring Security, and REST API design, to advanced subjects like Spring Boot Actuator, GraalVM native compilation, microservice patterns, and reactive programming with Spring WebFlux. Whether you are a Java fresher targeting your first enterprise role or a senior engineer interviewing for a tech lead position, this guide provides comprehensive Spring Boot interview preparation.

sections.heading: Why Spring Boot Dominates Enterprise Java Development
sections.content: Spring Boot's dominance in enterprise Java is the result of solving the right problems at the right time. When Spring Boot was released in 2014, enterprise Java development was synonymous with verbose XML configuration, complex WAR deployments to application servers, and hours of framework wiring before writing business logic. Spring Boot inverted this experience: a new project with full auto-configured infrastructure — embedded Tomcat server, JPA, security, logging, health checks — could be up and running in minutes with the Spring Initializr. This democratized enterprise Java development and has since powered millions of production applications. Spring Boot 3.x's support for GraalVM native image compilation transforms Java's traditional weakness (slow startup, high memory) into a strength: native Spring Boot applications start in milliseconds and use a fraction of the heap memory of JVM applications — making Java competitive with Go and Rust for serverless and cloud functions. Project Loom's virtual threads (stable in Java 21) enable writing synchronous-looking code that scales to massive concurrency without the complexity of reactive programming, potentially obsoleting Spring WebFlux for many use cases. For enterprises standardized on Java, Spring Boot's comprehensive ecosystem — Spring Security, Spring Data, Spring Cloud, Spring Batch, Spring Integration — provides a consistent, well-documented, enterprise-grade solution for virtually any backend use case.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for a Spring Boot Interview
sections.content: Spring Boot interview preparation requires covering the Spring Framework foundation as well as Spring Boot-specific features. Core Spring: Dependency Injection (DI) — inversion of control where the container manages object creation and wiring; constructor injection (preferred), setter injection, field injection (@Autowired). Bean lifecycle and scopes (singleton, prototype, request, session). Core annotations: @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Controller, @RestController, @Configuration, @Bean, @Autowired, @Qualifier, @Value, @Profile. Spring Boot specifics: auto-configuration mechanism (@SpringBootApplication = @Configuration + @EnableAutoConfiguration + @ComponentScan), Spring Boot starters (pre-configured dependency bundles like spring-boot-starter-web, spring-boot-starter-data-jpa), application.properties/application.yml configuration, profiles (@Profile, spring.profiles.active), and Actuator (/actuator/health, /actuator/metrics, /actuator/info, custom endpoints). Spring Data JPA: entity modeling with @Entity, @Id, @GeneratedValue, relationships (@OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @ManyToMany with @JoinTable), JpaRepository interface (CRUD + paging + sorting), derived query methods (findByLastName, findByAgeGreaterThan), @Query with JPQL or native SQL, @Transactional for transaction management. Spring Security: authentication (UserDetailsService, PasswordEncoder), authorization (method security with @PreAuthorize, URL security with SecurityFilterChain), JWT integration. Spring MVC REST: @RestController, @RequestMapping, @GetMapping/@PostMapping, @PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody, ResponseEntity.

sections.heading: Beginner Spring Boot Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Beginner Spring Boot questions establish foundational understanding of what Spring Boot is and its core concepts. Key beginner topics: what Spring Boot is (an opinionated framework that simplifies Spring application setup through auto-configuration and embedded servers), the difference between Spring Framework and Spring Boot (Spring is the core framework; Spring Boot provides auto-configuration, starters, and embedded servers on top of Spring), dependency injection and its benefits (loose coupling, testability, easier to swap implementations), the @SpringBootApplication annotation and what it does (combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan), creating a simple REST endpoint (@RestController + @GetMapping), the application.properties file and how to externalize configuration, Maven/Gradle build system basics for Spring Boot projects, and what Spring Initializr is. Common beginner stereotypes: @Service for business logic, @Repository for data access (also provides automatic exception translation), @Component for generic beans, @Controller for MVC controllers, @RestController for REST APIs (@Controller + @ResponseBody). The bean lifecycle: Spring creates beans, injects dependencies, calls @PostConstruct method, bean is ready, on shutdown calls @PreDestroy. Freshers should understand that Spring Boot's embedded server (Tomcat by default) means the application deploys as an executable JAR file — no separate application server required.

sections.heading: Intermediate Spring Boot Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Intermediate Spring Boot questions focus on Spring Data JPA, Spring Security, REST API design, and production-grade features. Spring Data JPA repository types: CrudRepository (basic CRUD), JpaRepository (extends PagingAndSortingRepository with flush and batch operations), and PagingAndSortingRepository (pagination and sorting). Pagination: Pageable parameter in repository methods, Page<T> return type, and PageRequest.of(pageNumber, pageSize, Sort.by('field')) usage. Transaction management: @Transactional annotation (applies ACID properties), propagation types (REQUIRED — default, joins existing or creates new; REQUIRES_NEW — always creates new, suspending current; SUPPORTS — runs in transaction if one exists), isolation levels (READ_COMMITTED default in most databases), and the transactional self-invocation problem (calling @Transactional method from the same class bypasses the proxy). Exception handling: @ControllerAdvice for global exception handling, @ExceptionHandler for specific exception types, returning proper HTTP status codes with ResponseEntity or @ResponseStatus. Validation: spring-boot-starter-validation, @Valid on @RequestBody, constraint annotations (@NotNull, @NotBlank, @Size, @Min, @Max, @Email, @Pattern), MethodArgumentNotValidException handling. DTOs vs entities: never expose JPA entities directly in REST responses — create DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) and use MapStruct for mapping.

sections.heading: Advanced Spring Boot Interview Questions Overview
sections.content: Advanced Spring Boot topics distinguish senior engineers. Spring Boot Actuator provides production-ready monitoring and management: /actuator/health (with custom health indicators), /actuator/metrics (JVM, HTTP, custom), /actuator/env (configuration properties), /actuator/loggers (dynamic log level changes), /actuator/threaddump, and /actuator/heapdump. Micrometer (Spring Boot's metrics facade) supports exporting to Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, and other observability platforms. Caching abstraction: @EnableCaching, @Cacheable (cache method results), @CachePut (update cache), @CacheEvict (invalidate cache), with Redis (spring-boot-starter-data-redis) as the distributed cache backend. Spring's event system: ApplicationEvent, @EventListener, ApplicationEventPublisher for decoupled component communication. Async processing: @EnableAsync + @Async annotation makes methods run in a thread pool executor — configure with ThreadPoolTaskExecutor. Virtual threads in Spring Boot 3.2+ (spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true) — thread-per-request model that scales like reactive without reactive complexity. Spring WebFlux for reactive programming: Mono (0-1 items), Flux (0-N items), reactive repositories with R2DBC, and the performance characteristics vs blocking MVC. Auto-configuration internals: @ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, @ConditionalOnProperty — Spring Boot only configures beans when conditions are met. Custom starters for sharing auto-configuration across projects.

sections.heading: Spring Boot Microservices and Cloud-Native Patterns
sections.content: Microservices architecture is a dominant topic in senior Spring Boot interviews. Spring Cloud provides the ecosystem for Spring Boot microservices: Spring Cloud Config (centralized configuration server), Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka or Spring Cloud Kubernetes (service discovery), Spring Cloud Gateway (API gateway with routing, rate limiting, authentication), Spring Cloud LoadBalancer (client-side load balancing), and Spring Cloud Sleuth/Micrometer Tracing (distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, Zipkin, Jaeger). Circuit breaker pattern with Resilience4j (resilience4j-spring-boot3 starter): @CircuitBreaker, @Retry, @RateLimiter, @Bulkhead annotations prevent cascade failures in distributed systems. Inter-service communication: synchronous via RestTemplate (legacy), WebClient (reactive), or OpenFeign (declarative HTTP client with @FeignClient); asynchronous via Spring Cloud Stream with Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ message brokers. The Saga pattern for distributed transactions across microservices (choreography-based with events vs orchestration-based with a saga orchestrator). Service mesh integration (Istio, Linkerd) for mTLS, traffic management, and observability at the infrastructure level. Docker containerization: multi-stage Dockerfile for Spring Boot, Spring Boot's buildpacks support (./mvnw spring-boot:build-image), and deploying to Kubernetes with liveness/readiness probes mapped to Actuator health endpoints.

content.conclusion: Spring Boot mastery is one of the most valuable and durable skills in enterprise software development. The framework's combination of productive defaults, comprehensive ecosystem, and enterprise reliability has made it the standard for Java backend development for a decade — and with Spring Boot 3.x's native image support, virtual thread integration, and observability improvements, it is well-positioned for the next decade. The 30 questions in this guide take you from Spring Boot fundamentals to advanced microservice patterns. To solidify your preparation, build a complete microservice with Spring Boot: implement a REST API with Spring MVC, secure it with Spring Security and JWT, use Spring Data JPA for persistence with proper transaction management, add Actuator endpoints for monitoring, write comprehensive tests with Spring Boot Test, containerize with Docker, and deploy to Kubernetes. This real-world practice makes the concepts concrete and gives you the specific examples that distinguish excellent interview candidates.

faq.question: What is the difference between @Component, @Service, and @Repository?
faq.answer: All three are specializations of @Component and cause the annotated class to be detected by component scanning and registered as a Spring bean. @Service has no additional functionality but semantically marks the class as a business service layer component. @Repository marks a data access object and additionally enables Spring's persistence exception translation — database-specific exceptions are translated into Spring's DataAccessException hierarchy. Use each according to the layer: @Repository for DAO/data access, @Service for business logic, @Component for any other Spring-managed component.

faq.question: What is Spring Boot auto-configuration and how does it work?
faq.answer: Auto-configuration automatically configures Spring beans based on what is on the classpath and what properties are set. @EnableAutoConfiguration (included in @SpringBootApplication) triggers the process. Spring Boot looks for auto-configuration classes listed in META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports. Each auto-configuration class uses @Conditional annotations (@ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, @ConditionalOnProperty) to only configure beans when specific conditions are met. For example, if JPA is on the classpath and no DataSource bean exists, Spring Boot auto-configures one from application.properties.

faq.question: What is the difference between @RestController and @Controller?
faq.answer: @Controller marks a class as an MVC controller that returns views (HTML) by default. Return values are resolved as view names via ViewResolver. To return data directly from a @Controller method, you add @ResponseBody to the method or the class. @RestController is a composed annotation (@Controller + @ResponseBody) — every method automatically serializes the return value to the HTTP response body (typically JSON via Jackson). Use @RestController for REST APIs that return data; use @Controller for traditional MVC applications returning HTML views.

faq.question: How does Spring Boot handle database transactions?
faq.answer: @Transactional marks a method or class for transactional execution — Spring creates a proxy that begins a transaction before the method and commits on success or rolls back on RuntimeException (unchecked) by default. Key attributes: propagation (REQUIRED joins existing or creates new; REQUIRES_NEW always creates new), isolation (READ_COMMITTED, REPEATABLE_READ, SERIALIZABLE), readOnly=true hint (optimizes read-only transactions), and rollbackFor (roll back on specific checked exceptions). Important: @Transactional does not work when calling the method from within the same class (self-invocation bypasses the proxy). Use AspectJ mode or refactor to a separate bean.

faq.question: What is Spring Boot Actuator and what does it provide?
faq.answer: Spring Boot Actuator adds production monitoring and management endpoints to Spring Boot applications. Key endpoints: /actuator/health (application health status with detailed component checks), /actuator/info (application info from application.properties), /actuator/metrics (JVM, HTTP, cache, database metrics via Micrometer), /actuator/env (active configuration and property sources), /actuator/loggers (view and change log levels at runtime), /actuator/threaddump (thread state snapshot), /actuator/heapdump (JVM heap dump). Secure sensitive endpoints (all except health and info by default require authentication). Integrate with Prometheus via /actuator/prometheus for metrics scraping.
